newsitem.title: UK: ATHLETICS-IAAF GIVES WILD CARDS TO WORLD CHAMPIONS.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-IAAF GIVES WILD CARDS TO WORLD CHAMPIONS.

text.p: The International Amateur Athletic Federation (IAAF) will allow reigning champions to compete at next month's world championships even if they have not been selected by their national federation.

The decision to give wild cards to defending champions was announced by the IAAF in Monaco on Monday. Double Olympic champion Michael Johnson will now be able to run at the Athens event although he missed the U.S. trials due to injury and was not selected for the American team.
Johnson won the 200 and 400 metres at the 1995 Gothenburg world championships and repeated the double at last year's Atlanta Olympics.
The ruling mainly affects the United States which has strict rules on qualification for major championships, allowing only the top three in the national trials to make the team.
But now Johnson, sprinters Gail Devers and Gwen Torrence plus decathlete Dan O'Brien, who all missed or failed to finish at the trials, will be allowed to take part.
Brad Hunt, the agent for Johnson, Torrence and O'Brien immediately confirmed that the trio would compete in Athens. "They will be there," he said.
